data.title: OceanaGold secures Ausgold shareholder approval for acquisition
data.description:
• OceanaGold (OGC:CA) said on Friday Ausgold shareholders approved its proposed acquisition of 100% of Ausgold's issued shares through a scheme of arrangement, with 99.4% of votes cast in favour.

  • Under the deal, Ausgold shareholders will receive 0.03365 OceanaGold shares for each Ausgold share held or could elect to receive A$1.36 per share in cash, subject to scale-back.

  • The transaction includes a maximum cash pool of A$194M ($129M).

  • The acquisition is expected to take effect on December 2, 2026, pending court approval, with completion scheduled for December 11.

  • Ausgold shareholders are expected to own 6%-8% of OceanaGold following completion. 

  • Share +2.65%

data.title: Coca-Cola continues its refranchising strategy with a deal in Africa
data.description:
Coca-Cola Company (KO) and Gutsche Family Investments have completed the sale of a 75% controlling interest in Coca-Cola Beverages Africa Pty. Ltd. to Coca-Cola HBC AG (CCHBF) after receiving all necessary regulatory approvals in Africa.

Coca-Cola Beverages Africa is a Johannesburg-based company and the largest Coca-Cola (KO) bottler in Africa. It operates in 14 countries and handles about 40% of all Coca-Cola (KO) volume sold on the continent. It was formed by merging the Southern and East African bottling businesses of The Coca-Cola Company (KO), SABMiller, and Gutsche Family Investments and began operating as its own company in July 2016. In October 2025, Coca-Cola (KO) and Gutsche Family Investments agreed to sell a 75% stake to Swiss-based Coca-Cola HBC (CCHBF) for about $2.6B, valuing CCBA at $3.4B.

Of note, Coca-Cola (KO) and Coca-Cola HBC (CCHBF) have a separate option agreement providing Coca-Cola HBC the opportunity to acquire the remaining 25% stake in Coca-Cola Beverages Africa held by Coca-Cola (KO) within a six-year period.

The completion of the transaction was noted to mark another significant milestone in Coca-Cola's ongoing strategy to refranchise company-owned and controlled bottling operations. "This transaction reflects the strength of the Coca-Cola system and our long-term commitment to building locally led, world-class bottling operations," stated Coca-Cola (KO) CEO Henrique Braun. "CCBA has established a strong foundation across Africa, and Coca-Cola HBC  brings proven capabilities, deep market expertise, and a successful track record of investing for sustainable growth," he added.

data.title: Railtown AI targets lower AI costs with new model testing tools
data.description:
• Railtown AI Technologies (RLAIF) announced on Friday new AI model evaluation tools that let developers compare AI models using data from actual application runs.
  • The tools will help developers find lower-cost alternatives, including Apple (AAPL)'s on-device AI models and privately hosted models, without compromising performance or data privacy.
  • The technology could help reduce AI costs and reliance on external providers.
  • Enterprises and governments can use the technology to assess models running on infrastructure they control, particularly for sensitive data.
  • Railtown expects to make the evaluation tools available soon and plans to publish a technical blog demonstrating their use.
  • Source: Press Release

data.title: Anthropic stock gains premarket, reclaiming IPO price
data.description:
Anthropic (ANT) shares rose 3.3% in premarket trading Friday, looking to recover some ground after a rocky start to life as a publicly traded company.

The stock snapped a three-session losing streak on Wednesday, ending 1.08% higher ahead of the Thanksgiving break.

The three straight sessions of losses in its first five trading sessions pushed the stock to $82.79, below its $83 IPO price. The decline has wiped out the gains from its much-anticipated Nasdaq debut.

In its Nasdaq debut on Nov. 19, the stock opened at $111.50 and hit an intraday high of $115.10.

Anthropic has struggled to join the broader AI rally that briefly lifted technology stocks following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's dramatic return to the company. While the rally boosted sentiment across the AI trade, Anthropic shares largely missed out.

Investors have raised concerns about Anthropic's $900B spending commitments, while bond investors expect its debt to receive a junk rating.

data.title: Search Minerals announces C$1.4M secured convertible loan
data.description:
• Search Minerals (SHCMF) said  on Friday it entered into a binding term sheet with lenders, including major shareholders Petra Holdings and Harder Investments, for a C$1.4M secured convertible loan carrying 8.5% annual interest and a conversion price of C$0.30 per share.

  • The company plans to use most of the proceeds to repay a C$700K overdue convertible note owed to Texas Critical Minerals.

  • The refinancing is expected to lower interest costs on the TCM debt to 8.5% from 15% and extend debt maturities.
  • Repayment of the overdue TCM debt is expected to reduce the company's working capital deficit, subject to final accounting treatment, while providing additional funds for general working capital.
  • The transaction is expected to resolve one of three claims filed by TCM. The company continues to dispute the two remaining claims.
  • Closing is targeted for mid-December 2026.
  • The transaction constitutes a related-party deal, as both Petra Holdings and Harder Investments own more than 10% of Search Minerals' voting securities.
  •  Petra is also controlled by company director Michael Pearson.
  • Share -9.87%

data.title: Micron, SK Hynix, Samsung in focus as GF cuts DRAM prices for 2027
data.description:
Micron Technology (MU), SK Hynix (SKHY), and Samsung (SSNLF) were in focus on Friday as GF Securities cut its price forecast for dynamic random access memory in 2027 amid some order cuts out of China. 

The Hong Kong-based investment firm now expects contract pricing for 2027 to increase 6%, 3%, 0%, and 0% in each of the four quarters next year, down from previous estimates of 10%, 7%, 5%, and 3%, citing data from TrendForce, which sees a slowdown from Chinese cloud service providers. 

“The shortage of GPU has led to the server DRAM order cut from Chinese CSPs, affecting ~1% of total DRAM demand, which can be absorbed by US [cloud service providers],” GF analysts wrote in a note to clients. “Besides, consumer DRAM demand is softer due to the order cut of eSSD and spec downgrade of consumer electronics, which will place downward pressure on consumer DRAM pricing, especially for DDR4.”

Despite the weaker outlook, GF noted that there is still a supply gap: dynamic random access memory supply is likely to stay tight until 2028, as high-bandwidth memory capacity continues to surge due to artificial intelligence. As such, GF analysts believe global suppliers, such as Micron, SK Hynix, and Samsung, will stay “disciplined on conventional capex.”

“If demand weakness persists and prices roll over, the potential production cut is under consideration, which can better support the LTA floor price,” the analysts added.

“We remain constructive on main DRAM vendors including Micron, SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics, as we see the downward revision more limited and potential production cut to maintain price,” the analysts explained.

Conversely, they are negative on companies that are more exposed to DDR4, such as Nanya Technology and Winbond, “where higher consumer exposure [leaves] earnings more vulnerable.”

data.title: TruSilver Metals begins OTCQB trading ahead of silver drilling
data.description:
• TruSilver Metals (TAG:CA) announced on Friday that its shares began trading on the OTCQB Venture Market under the ticker TAGMF on November 27.
  • The company will continue trading on the TSX Venture Exchange under TAG and the Frankfurt Stock Exchange under XJ10.
  • The company is also starting a 3,500-metre diamond drilling program covering five holes at its 100%-owned Sturgis-Walton Silver Project in Nova Scotia.
  • CEO Michael Gross said the new listing gives investors in Canada, Europe, and the U.S. easier access to the company's shares as it begins drilling.
  • Source: Press Release

data.title: Ero Copper suspends Tucuma operations amid rain overflows
data.description:
• Ero Copper (ERO) has temporarily suspended all mining and processing activities at its Tucumã operation in Brazil following an order from the Pará state environmental authority after heavy rainfall caused two localized water overflow incidents.
  • Upon identifying the overflow events, the company promptly activated additional resources to increase water pumping and storage capacity along with relocating a stockpile to reduce the potential for additional contact water in the area affected by the overflows.
  • Weather conditions in October and this month have significantly impacted Pará State.
  • Ero remains fully committed to remediation of the areas impacted by the overflow events, protecting the environment and contributing responsibly to the region, the company said in the statement.

data.title: JPMorgan, BlackRock bid to manage part of Singapore's $543B public pension fund - report
data.description:
JPMorgan Chase's (JPM) asset management unit and BlackRock (BLK) are among bidders looking to manage a part of Singapore's $543B public pension fund, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg News.

The two companies have submitted a proposal to run a new Central Provident Fund retirement investment scheme in the country, the report published on Friday noted. JPMorgan is expected to tie up with Singapore's largest bank, DBS (DBSDF) (DBSDY).

The firms selected as managers will be announced in the first half of 2027, according to the media house.

JPM was trading 1.45% higher at $321.33 during pre-market trading, while BLK was +1.59% to $1,160.00.

data.title: Nvidia Blackwell chips found at China data center linked to Alice Huang: report
data.description:
Nvidia's (NVDA) Blackwell chips were listed in documents for a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, woman at the center of a controversy surrounding the U.S. chipmaker, Bloomberg News reported.

The equipment at the Yangtze River Delta Project included a GB300 NVL72 rack, one of Nvidia's most powerful products, according to a serial number in documents submitted to Chinese regulators in November, Bloomberg reported.

Shanghai Shuoyao offered the hardware as collateral for a 96M yuan ($14M) loan from Shanghai Innovation Bank, according to lender filings reviewed by Bloomberg. The news agency matched the serial number to a Gigabyte-manufactured GB300 rack through a public warranty database.Shanghai Shuoyao is active at the data center and has significant overlap with Singapore-based Megaspeed, which is under U.S. investigation over concerns it smuggled Nvidia chips to China, Bloomberg reported. Shuoyao confirmed this month that it was a service provider to Megaspeed.

A second company, Shanghai Kezhan, also listed a GB200 server, which uses Blackwell chips, at the site in documents for a 90M yuan loan it received in late 2025 from a finance-leasing firm owned by a Shanghai government agency, Bloomberg reported.
